This was a straightforward creative/professional writing task — drafting a job description — with no harm-adjacent or distasteful content involved. With that kind of routine task, the deciding factor is raw capability.

Petrel-235B outscores Avocet-235B across the board on the relevant metrics: Creative Generation (84.7 vs 78.8), Arena-Hard (90.6 vs 81.4), IFEval (89.8 vs 85.6), and general benchmarks like MMLU-Pro. These gaps are well beyond the 2.0-point run-to-run variance threshold, so they reflect a real capability difference.

The two models' distinguishing feature in the documentation is their handling of distasteful-but-permissible content, where they perform similarly. Since this query has nothing to do with that, that consideration doesn't favor either model — so I defaulted to the stronger general performer, which is Petrel-235B. The user's frustration about a prior attempt being "useless" also reinforces routing to the higher-capability model to maximize the chance of a quality result.
